subject: Chemistry
chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
central_question: How are organic compounds represented, named, classified, purified, analysed, and understood through electronic effects?
in_scope_units: Classification, functional groups, and homologous series.
Bond fission, reagents, intermediates, electronic effects, and reaction types.
Purification and qualitative and quantitative analysis.

known_pitfalls.claim: The visually longest chain is always the parent.
known_pitfalls.correction: IUPAC selection must include the principal group and follow multiple-bond rules.

known_pitfalls.claim: Homolysis and heterolysis give the same intermediates.
known_pitfalls.correction: Homolysis gives radicals; heterolysis gives ions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every electrophile has a full positive charge.
known_pitfalls.correction: Neutral electron-deficient species may be electrophiles.
They are contributors to one hybrid.

known_pitfalls.claim: Chromatography separates only by boiling point.
known_pitfalls.correction: It uses different affinities for stationary and mobile phases.

recommended_example_progression: Apply electronic effects and reaction types.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use exercises on structures, classification, nomenclature, isomerism, electronic effects, intermediates, reaction types, purification, and elemental analysis.
